literature.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒暴发凸显非洲公共卫生系统脆弱性。
literature.lead_zh: 近期非洲多国出现马尔堡病毒疫情,揭示了全球卫生安全和疫情应对中的结构性不平等。
key_findings_zh: 马尔堡病毒在非洲多国暴发,暴露了卫生系统在资源分配和伦理保护方面的不足 [10.1136/bmjgh-2026-025630]。
疫情应对中,医护人员面临持续的心理和伦理压力 [10.1136/bmjgh-2026-025630]。
疫苗接种对控制马尔堡病毒传播具有显著效果 [10.1016/j.nxmate.2026.103628]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 马尔堡病毒的持续传播和疫情暴发风险提示全球卫生安全体系需加强伦理和结构韧性。
literature.caveats_zh: 研究基于定性分析,缺乏实际数据支持。
literature.headline_en: Marburg Virus Outbreak Highlights Structural Vulnerabilities in African Public Health Systems.
literature.lead_en: Recent outbreaks of Marburg virus in Africa reveal the fragility of global health security and structural inequities in epidemic response.
key_findings_en: Marburg virus outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda expose weaknesses in health system resilience and ethical protections [10.1136/bmjgh-2026-025630]
Frontline healthcare workers face ongoing psychological and ethical burdens during the outbreak [10.1136/bmjgh-2026-025630]
Vaccination significantly reduces the spread of Marburg virus in simulated scenarios [10.1016/j.nxmate.2026.103628]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The persistent spread of Marburg virus and its outbreak potential highlight the need for improved global health security frameworks.
literature.caveats_en: The study relies on numerical simulations and lacks real-world data.
literature.brief_en: Recent Marburg virus outbreaks in Africa reveal systemic vulnerabilities in health systems and the importance of vaccination in controlling transmission.

papers.full_text: ConclusionRecent outbreaks across Africa demonstrate that emerging infectious disease crises are not only biomedical events but recurring ethical and political stress tests for national health systems and global health governance. From West Africa to the DRC and East Africa, frontline healthcare workers have repeatedly been asked to confront extraordinary risks while operating within systems marked by inequity, scarcity and institutional fragility.The ethical dilemmas observed across Ebola, Marburg and COVID-19 responses show that epidemic preparedness cannot be reduced to surveillance systems, laboratory capacity and emergency containment strategies. Ethical preparedness, including workforce protection, transparent decision-making, reciprocal institutional obligations, psychosocial support and meaningful community engagement, must become central to global health security frameworks.Without sustained investment in resilient and equitable health systems, outbreaks will continue to place disproportionate moral and physical burdens on frontline healthcare workers. The true measure of preparedness is not only the capacity to contain outbreaks rapidly but also the ability of health systems to protect the dignity, safety and moral agency of the healthcare workers and communities expected to sustain the response. Embedded empirical ethics networks, integrated within health systems and research programmes, offer a promising mechanism for operationalising ethical preparedness.By building relationships, contextual knowledge and analytical capacity during interepidemic periods, such networks can support rapid, context-sensitive analysis of ethical trade-offs as well as ethical decision-making when crises emerge. As global health governance increasingly operates within a fractured global order, ethical preparedness cannot remain dependent on unstable cycles of outbreak response and short-term international solidarity. It must be embedded in the ordinary architecture of health systems before the next crisis begins. Introduction The resurgence of viral haemorrhagic fevers across Africa underscores the fragility of global health security and the persistent ethical vulnerabilities facing frontline healthcare workers. Recurrent outbreaks of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda, alongside Marburg virus disease alerts in several African countries, show how rapidly localised epidemics can become regional and international public health threats.1 2 These crises reveal that high-consequence infectious disease outbreaks are not isolated national emergencies. They are interconnected global health challenges that expose structural inequities in preparedness, response and health system resilience.3 4These vulnerabilities are unfolding within a shifting international political and economic order. The move from aid-centred global health engagement towards the growing ‘prominence of trade objectives’ occurs in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.5 While such transitions may create opportunities for economic advancement, they also risk deepening the vulnerability of health systems already strained by historical underinvestment, debt burdens, workforce shortages and uneven infrastructure development.6 Under these conditions, epidemic response capacity cannot be separated from broader questions of global justice and the distribution of institutional resilience.Recent Ebola outbreaks in the DRC and Uganda, together with recurring Marburg virus disease threats, continue to expose ethical and structural weaknesses in post-COVID-19 health systems. Even outbreaks that remain relatively contained impose substantial moral and occupational burdens on healthcare workers operating within fragile institutions.7 Across recurrent epidemics, the foundational pillars of resilient health systems—workforce capacity, infection prevention infrastructure, essential medicines, financing, governance and community trust—remain uneven and often inadequate.8 9Frontline healthcare workers are therefore required to navigate competing obligations to patients, families, colleagues, communities and themselves while often lacking adequate institutional protection. The ethical dilemmas they face extend beyond clinical decision-making. They include questions of professional duty amid personal risk, justice in resource allocation, reciprocity between institutions and workers, community trust and the psychological consequences of sustained moral distress.7 10 These challenges are amplified in contexts where historical neglect, underinvestment and inequitable global responses have eroded confidence in public institutions.This commentary argues that ethical preparedness must become a central component of epidemic response. Without transparent decision-making processes, reciprocal institutional support, and meaningful community engagement, outbreak responses risk collapsing under the weight of moral uncertainty, endangering both healthcare workers and the populations they serve. Ethical preparedness and the limits of the duty to careEmerging infectious disease outbreaks expose a fundamental tension within healthcare professionalism: the expectation that healthcare workers will continue delivering care despite substantial personal risk. During outbreaks of highly infectious diseases, frontline healthcare workers are expected to uphold beneficence while facing threats to their own safety, their families and their communities. Yet the ethical legitimacy of this expectation depends on whether institutions and governments fulfil reciprocal obligations to protect them.In many low-resource settings, this reciprocity remains incomplete. Personal protective equipment, infection prevention infrastructure, laboratory capacity, workforce surge mechanisms and occupational protections are often insufficient during epidemic escalation. Under such conditions, the duty to care risks becoming less a professional obligation grounded in mutual trust and more a form of institutionalised sacrifice.11 The ethical question is therefore not simply whether healthcare workers should respond during outbreaks, but whether health systems have done enough to justify asking them to assume extraordinary risks.During Ebola outbreaks in West Africa and the DRC, frontline healthcare workers experienced disproportionate infection and mortality, reflecting systemic failures in preparedness rather than individual shortcomings. Similar patterns emerged during COVID-19, when health systems worldwide relied on professional altruism to compensate for chronic underinvestment in workforce protection. The repeated normalisation of healthcare worker sacrifice reveals a dangerous assumption within global health governance: that resilience can substitute for structural support.Ethical preparedness must therefore be understood as a core pillar of epidemic preparedness. Protecting healthcare workers requires more than emergency procurement once crises begin. It demands sustained investment in workforce safety, fair compensation, mental health services, safe working conditions, transparent institutional accountability and mechanisms for worker participation in planning and response. Without these safeguards, healthcare workers are left to absorb the moral and physical costs of systemic fragility. Resource allocation, structural inequity and procedural justiceOutbreak settings frequently force healthcare workers to make decisions under profound scarcity. In fragile health systems, triage extends beyond clinical prioritisation and becomes a reflection of deeper structural inequities. Decisions about access to isolation units, supportive therapies, referral pathways, diagnostics and critical care resources are often shaped by geography, socioeconomic status, infrastructure and political marginalisation rather than clinical need alone.The ethical principle of justice requires that scarce resources be allocated fairly and transparently.12 However, operationalising justice during epidemics is especially difficult where baseline inequities already shape health outcomes. Patients from remote or underserved communities may present later because of transportation barriers, mistrust, delayed surveillance or weak referral systems. As a result, they may appear clinically ‘less likely’ to survive. Strict utilitarian frameworks that prioritise those with the highest probability of survival may therefore systematically disadvantage populations already excluded from equitable healthcare access.These dilemmas show why ethical decision-making during outbreaks cannot rely solely on abstract triage principles imported from high-resource settings. Ethical frameworks must account for the historical and structural conditions that shape vulnerability. Procedural justice is essential. This includes transparent triage criteria, multidisciplinary decision-making, documentation of decisions, appeals processes where feasible, and community-informed accountability mechanisms.13Frontline healthcare workers often shoulder these decisions without adequate institutional guidance. The psychological burden of repeated moral compromise contributes to burnout, moral injury and long-term workforce attrition. Ethical preparedness therefore requires not only technical triage protocols but also systems that distribute responsibility collectively rather than leaving individual providers isolated in impossible decision-making environments. Community trust as a foundation of epidemic responseOutbreak control depends not only on biomedical interventions but also on public trust. Experiences from Ebola and COVID-19 responses show that containment measures imposed without meaningful community engagement can generate resistance, misinformation and social fragmentation. Quarantine, safe burial protocols, movement restrictions, case investigation and surveillance may be epidemiologically justified, yet they can also reproduce histories of exclusion, coercion and institutional distrust.In many epidemic settings, frontline healthcare workers become the visible face of state authority and international response efforts. This places them in ethically complex positions as both caregivers and enforcers of public health interventions. The resulting tension can erode relationships between communities and health systems, particularly where previous experiences of neglect or political marginalisation remain unresolved.Community engagement should therefore be understood not merely as a communication strategy but as an ethical commitment grounded in respect, transparency and shared decision-making. Ethical engagement requires moving beyond transactional messaging towards genuine partnership with affected communities. This includes involving local leaders, women’s groups, faith-based organisations, youth representatives, survivors and traditional healers in planning and implementation.13Trust cannot be improvised during emergencies. It reflects longstanding relationships between institutions and communities. Epidemic responses that fail to acknowledge historical grievances risk deepening suspicion and undermining compliance. Ethical outbreak governance therefore depends on sustained investment in community-centred health systems long before crises emerge. Moral distress, institutional betrayal and workforce sustainabilityThe psychological consequences of epidemic response among frontline healthcare workers remain insufficiently addressed in global health preparedness frameworks. Repeated exposure to death, fear of infection, prolonged separation from family, stigmatisation and the emotional burden of triage decision-making contribute to moral distress and burnout. These experiences intensify when healthcare workers believe institutions have failed to provide adequate protection or support.A central ethical concern is the reciprocity deficit between healthcare systems and their workforce. During outbreaks, healthcare workers are frequently praised as heroes while working without adequate protective equipment, reliable salaries, psychosocial support, rest periods or safe working conditions. This disconnect creates a form of institutional betrayal: workers are expected to demonstrate extraordinary commitment while the systems that employ them fail to meet corresponding obligations.These conditions have implications beyond individual well-being. Workforce burnout undermines epidemic response capacity, weakens health system resilience and contributes to long-term attrition in already understaffed systems. Ethical preparedness must therefore include workforce sustainability as a central objective, not a secondary consideration.Health systems and international partners should institutionalise psychological support services, peer-support structures, adequate rest periods and occupational protections as standard components of outbreak response.14 Equally important is the need for visible institutional accountability. Acknowledging failures in worker protection and taking corrective action are essential to rebuilding trust within the health workforce. From ethical principles to implementation: governance and financingEthical preparedness will remain aspirational unless its requirements are translated into routine institutional arrangements before outbreaks occur. Health ministries and healthcare institutions should establish standing ethics preparedness structures linked to emergency preparedness committees, with clear authority to develop context-specific guidance on duty to care, workforce protection, triage, compensation, community engagement and psychosocial support. In other words, these structures would help make ethical decisions in the midst of changing circumstances, pressing deadlines, uncertainty and danger. Frontline healthcare workers and community representatives would be included in these structures and use transparent decision-making procedures as well as conduct periodic preparedness exercises so that ethical guidance is available before scarcity and uncertainty intensify during an emergency.9 13Implementation also requires durable ethics capacity rather than ad hoc consultation during crises. One practical model is the establishment of embedded empirical ethics networks within health and research systems.15 By identifying emerging ethical challenges in real time, supporting transparent decision-making during crises, documenting and addressing moral distress among frontline workers and facilitating community engagement and accountability, such networks can contribute directly to ethical preparedness. This embedded capacity connects analysis of ethical trade-offs to operational realities, providing an institutional mechanism for translating principles into locally appropriate decisions.Financing these measures raises a distributive justice question: the costs should not fall solely on resource-constrained facilities, frontline workers or countries facing recurrent outbreaks. National governments retain primary responsibility for core health-system functions and should incorporate workforce protection, infection prevention, occupational health, psychosocial services and ethics preparedness into routine health and emergency budgets. However, where fiscal capacity is insufficient, regional bodies, bilateral and multilateral partners, global health security initiatives and research funders also have reciprocal responsibilities to provide predictable and additional support, particularly where outbreak control generates regional and global public goods.4 8 Funding arrangements should therefore move away from short-term emergency procurement towards multiyear preparedness financing, with explicit budget lines, transparent allocation criteria and accountability for whether promised protections reach frontline services.This approach does not eliminate the need for priority-setting. In severely constrained settings, not every preparedness measure can be implemented simultaneously. Governments and partners should therefore use transparent, participatory priority-setting to protect a minimum package of essential obligations first: reliable infection prevention and personal protective equipment, occupational protections and compensation, psychosocial support, fair triage processes and mechanisms for worker and community participation. The ethical requirement is not unlimited expenditure but a defensible process in which the level of protection expected from healthcare workers is matched by proportionate institutional and international commitments to reduce avoidable risk. papers.title: Psychosocial impact of Marburg virus disease on recovered individuals and frontline health workers in Rwanda: a cross-sectional survey.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine the psychosocial impact of this disease on recovered individuals and frontline health workers (FHWs) following the 2024 MVD outbreak in Rwanda. DESIGN: a cross-sectional survey. SETTING: Kigali, the capital city of Rwanda, had two treatment centres during the outbreak of the MVD disease from 24 September to 24 October 2024. PARTICIPANTS: All 51 recovered individuals from MVD and 98 FHWs who met the eligibility criteria were involved in the study.Depression was measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), anxiety with the Generalised Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) scale and post-traumatic stress disorder using the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Perceived stigma was measured using the adapted Ebola stigma and discrimination questionnaire and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support Scale (MPSS) to assess social support. Wilcoxon rank-sum and Kruskal-Wallis tests examined differences in depression, anxiety and PTSD by sex and profession. Spearman correlation assessed relationships between variables. RESULTS: 115 participants, including 29 recovered people and 86 FHWs. 11.8% of FHWs had moderate to severe depression and 20.7% of recovered people had mild to moderate depression. Moderate to severe anxiety was exhibited by 9.4% of FHWs, and mild anxiety was reported by 17.2% of recovered people. 9.3% of FHWs and one recovered individual had a total PCL score above 33 (PTSD). Among recovered people, there was a significant negative correlation between anxiety and social support (r=-0.36, p value=0.05) and a significant difference in PTSD symptom levels between sexes (p value=0.01). Among FHWs, MVD-related stigma was positively correlated with PTSD symptoms (r=+0.23, p value=0.05). Symptoms of depression (β coef.=-0.19, 95% CI -0.32, -0.05) and anxiety (β coef.=-0.16, 95% CI -0.26, -0.06) decreased with age. Married FHWs had lower levels of depression (β coef.=-2.72, 95% CI -4.96, -0.49) and anxiety (β coef.=-2.35, 95% CI -4.07, -0.62) compared with single individuals. CONCLUSION: Six months post-containment of the MVD outbreak in Rwanda, many FHWs were still experiencing depression, anxiety and PTSD. Contextualised and culturally adapted mental health and psychosocial support interventions are highly recommended for integration into infectious disease response plans.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the psychosocial impact of Marburg virus disease on recovered individuals and frontline health workers in Rwanda following the 2024 outbreak. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in Kigali, involving 51 recovered individuals and 98 frontline health workers. Mental health was assessed using PHQ-9, GAD-7, and PCL-5, while stigma and social support were evaluated with adapted questionnaires. Results showed that 11.8% of frontline health workers had moderate to severe depression, and 20.7% of recovered individuals had mild to moderate depression. Anxiety and PTSD symptoms were also observed, with significant correlations between stigma and PTSD in frontline workers and between anxiety and social support in recovered individuals. The study's cross-sectional design limits its ability to establish causality, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength due to self-reported data and potential biases.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨2024年MVD 暴发后,马尔堡病毒病对卢旺达康复者及一线医护人员的心理社会影响。研究动机源于了解该疾病对受影响人群心理健康后果的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在卢旺达首都基加利进行了一项横断面调查,该城市在2024年9月24日至10月24日的MVD 暴发期间设有两个治疗中心。所有符合纳入标准的51名MVD康复者和98名一线医护人员均被纳入研究。
elements_zh.methods: 使用患者健康问卷(PHQ-9)评估抑郁,使用广泛性焦虑障碍量表(GAD-7)评估焦虑,使用DSM-5创伤后应激障碍检查清单(PCL-5)评估创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)。使用改编版埃博拉病毒污名与歧视问卷评估感知污名,使用多维社会支持感知量表(MPSS)评估社会支持。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究共纳入115名参与者,包括29名康复者和86名一线医护人员。在一线医护人员中,11.8%有中度至重度抑郁,20.7%的康复者有轻度至中度抑郁。9.4%的一线医护人员报告有中度至重度焦虑,而17.2%的康复者有轻度焦虑。1名康复者和9.3%的一线医护人员总PCL评分超过33分,表明存在PTSD。在康复者中,焦虑与社会支持之间存在显著负相关(r=-0.36,p值=0.05),且性别间PTSD症状水平存在显著差异(p值=0.01)。在一线医护人员中,与MVD相关的污名与PTSD症状呈显著正相关(r=+0.23,p值=0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,卢旺达MVD 暴发被控制六个月后,许多一线医护人员仍经历抑郁、焦虑和PTSD。他们强调了研究的新颖性,即关注马尔堡病毒病对康复者和医护人员的心理社会影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,应将心理健康和心理社会支持干预措施纳入传染病应对计划,以应对受影响个体和医护人员持续的心理负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法进行因果推断。由于依赖自我报告测量和调查环境中的潜在偏倚,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨2024年MVD 暴发后,马尔堡病毒病对卢旺达康复者及一线医护人员的心理社会影响。研究动机源于了解该疾病对受影响人群心理健康后果的必要性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在卢旺达首都基加利进行了一项横断面调查,该城市在2024年9月24日至10月24日的MVD 暴发期间设有两个治疗中心。所有符合纳入标准的51名MVD康复者和98名一线医护人员均被纳入研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用患者健康问卷(PHQ-9)评估抑郁,使用广泛性焦虑障碍量表(GAD-7)评估焦虑,使用DSM-5创伤后应激障碍检查清单(PCL-5)评估创伤后应激障碍(PTSD)。使用改编版埃博拉病毒污名与歧视问卷评估感知污名,使用多维社会支持感知量表(MPSS)评估社会支持。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究共纳入115名参与者,包括29名康复者和86名一线医护人员。在一线医护人员中,11.8%有中度至重度抑郁,20.7%的康复者有轻度至中度抑郁。9.4%的一线医护人员报告有中度至重度焦虑,而17.2%的康复者有轻度焦虑。1名康复者和9.3%的一线医护人员总PCL评分超过33分,表明存在PTSD。在康复者中,焦虑与社会支持之间存在显著负相关(r=-0.36,p值=0.05),且性别间PTSD症状水平存在显著差异(p值=0.01)。在一线医护人员中,与MVD相关的污名与PTSD症状呈显著正相关(r=+0.23,p值=0.05)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,卢旺达MVD 暴发被控制六个月后,许多一线医护人员仍经历抑郁、焦虑和PTSD。他们强调了研究的新颖性,即关注马尔堡病毒病对康复者和医护人员的心理社会影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,应将心理健康和心理社会支持干预措施纳入传染病应对计划,以应对受影响个体和医护人员持续的心理负担。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计,无法进行因果推断。由于依赖自我报告测量和调查环境中的潜在偏倚,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Machine learning-enhanced stochastic modeling of Marburg virus transmission in human–bat populations
papers.abstract: A serious threat to global health is the Marburg virus, which affects human beings as well as non-human primates. This study develops a comprehensive stochastic mathematical model to examine Marburg virus transmission dynamics in human and bat populations, incorporating vaccination effects and random environmental factors including immigration, climate change, and behavioral variations. In this work, we employ stochastic differential equations coupled with neural network analysis to capture the complex disease dynamics. First, we prove that the solution exists globally and is positive. Next, we establish the fundamental stochastic reproduction number, which serves as a threshold parameter determining disease extinction ( R 0 s 1 ) in the population. Numerical simulation is performed to investigate the dynamics of Marburg virus disease in the population. Numerical simulation shows that as value of vaccination increases, it leads to decreases in the spread of Marburg virus. This shows that vaccination is very important to control the spread of Marburg virus in the community. A feedforward neural network (FFNN) is employed as a surrogate model and trained using the numerical solution generated by the Euler–Maruyama scheme. The network learns a continuous nonlinear mapping from simulation time to the corresponding compartmental states, thereby providing a smooth approximation of the realized stochastic trajectory. The simulated dataset is randomly divided into training (70%), validation (15%), and testing (15%) subsets. The accuracy of Neural Networks in prediction and modeling is demonstrated by dividing the data into 70% for training, 15% for testing, and 15% for validation. Validating its accuracy, the model attains a mean squared error of 2.39 × 10−4 averaged over the eight compartments and a regression coefficient close to one (R = 0.999). The results of this study offer public health strategists effective tools for reducing or eliminating Marburg virus.

In this work, we employ stochastic differential equations coupled with neural network analysis to capture the complex disease dynamics. First, we prove that the solution exists globally and is positive. Next, we establish the fundamental stochastic reproduction number, which serves as a threshold parameter determining disease extinction ( R 0 s 1 ) in the population. Numerical simulation is performed to investigate the dynamics of Marburg virus disease in the population. Numerical simulation shows that as value of vaccination increases, it leads to decreases in the spread of Marburg virus. This shows that vaccination is very important to control the spread of Marburg virus in the community. A feedforward neural network (FFNN) is employed as a surrogate model and trained using the numerical solution generated by the Euler–Maruyama scheme. The network learns a continuous nonlinear mapping from simulation time to the corresponding compartmental states, thereby providing a smooth approximation of the realized stochastic trajectory. The simulated dataset is randomly divided into training (70%), validation (15%), and testing (15%) subsets. The accuracy of Neural Networks in prediction and modeling is demonstrated by dividing the data into 70% for training, 15% for testing, and 15% for validation. Validating its accuracy, the model attains a mean squared error of 2.39 × 10−4 averaged over the eight compartments and a regression coefficient close to one (R = 0.999). The results of this study offer public health strategists effective tools for reducing or eliminating Marburg virus.

papers.abstract_zh: 对全球健康构成严重威胁的是马尔堡病毒,它影响着人类以及非人灵长类动物。本研究开发了一个全面的随机数学模型,用于考察马尔堡病毒在人类和蝙蝠种群中的动态变化,包括疫苗接种效应以及随机环境因素,如移民、气候变化和行为变化。在本工作中,我们采用随机微分方程结合神经网络分析来捕捉疾病的复杂动态。首先,我们证明了解在全局范围内存在且为正。接下来,我们建立了基本的随机再生数,该参数作为决定疾病在种群中灭绝(R 0 s 1)的阈值参数。通过数值模拟来研究马尔堡病毒病在种群中的动态变化。数值模拟结果表明,随着疫苗接种值的增加,会导致马尔堡病毒传播的减少。这表明疫苗接种对于控制马尔堡病毒在社区中的传播非常重要。采用前馈神经网络(FFNN)作为替代模型,并使用欧拉-马尔永方案生成的数值解进行训练。该网络学习从模拟时间到相应隔室状态的连续非线性映射,从而提供随机轨迹的平滑近似。模拟数据集被随机划分为训练集(70%)、验证集(15%)和测试集(15%)。通过将数据划分为70%用于训练、15%用于测试和15%用于验证,展示了神经网络在预测和建模方面的准确性。验证其准确性,该模型在八个隔室上的均方误差平均为2.39 × 10−4,回归系数接近1(R = 0.999)。本研究的结果为公共卫生策略制定者提供了有效工具,以减少或消除马尔堡病毒。

papers.title: Proteomic comparison of Marburg and Kasokero virus infection in natural host Egyptian rousette bat reveals distinct antiviral pathways
papers.abstract: Abstract Bats are natural reservoir hosts for numerous zoonotic viruses, yet the molecular mechanisms enabling viral persistence without overt disease remain incompletely understood. The Egyptian rousette bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus, ERB) is the sole known natural reservoir of Marburg virus (MARV) and a key host in the enzootic cycle of the tick-borne Kasokero virus (KASV), providing a unique system to compare host responses to different RNA viruses within the same species. Here, we applied serial cross-sectional serum proteomics integrated with tissue-specific viral kinetics to characterize systemic host responses to experimental MARV and KASV infection in captive-reared bats. Nearly 16 % of detected proteins (67/419) were found exclusively in infected animals, yet canonical acute inflammatory signatures driving pathology in other susceptible hosts were absent (e.g., in humans and non-human primates). Differential abundance and detection analyses identified both shared and virus-dependent responses, with MARV infection eliciting limited and transient perturbations, while KASV induced broader and more sustained engagement of complement, lectin pathway, and hepatometabolic proteins. Network-based analysis uncovered coordinated proteasome modules — including circulating immunoproteasome complexes — consistent with enhanced antigen-processing capacity is a feature of these virus-host dynamics. Together, these findings reveal how ERBs mount structured, virus-dependent systemic responses, offering new insight into mechanisms underlying viral infection in natural reservoir hosts.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the molecular mechanisms that allow viral persistence in natural host Egyptian rousette bats without causing overt disease, particularly focusing on Marburg virus and its related tick-borne counterpart Kasokero virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved experimental infections of captive-reared Egyptian rousette bats with Marburg virus (MARV) and Kasokero virus (KASV), using serial cross-sectional serum proteomics and tissue-specific viral kinetics to analyze host responses.
analysis.methods: The researchers integrated serial cross-sectional serum proteomics with tissue-specific viral kinetics to characterize systemic host responses to experimental MARV and KASV infections in captive-reared bats.
analysis.main_results: Nearly 16 % of detected proteins (67/419) were found exclusively in infected animals, yet canonical acute inflammatory signatures typically associated with disease in other hosts were absent. MARV infection caused limited and transient perturbations, while KASV induced broader and more sustained engagement of complement, lectin pathway, and hepatometabolic proteins.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Egyptian rousette bats mount structured, virus-dependent systemic responses to MARV and KASV, highlighting distinct antiviral pathways that may contribute to their role as natural reservoirs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide new insights into the mechanisms of viral infection in natural reservoir hosts, which could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and prevention strategies for Marburg virus disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on captive-reared bats and the absence of direct comparisons with other related viruses, but the evidence is strong due to the integration of proteomics and viral kinetics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying viral persistence in Egyptian rousette bats, the sole natural reservoir of Marburg virus (MARV). By comparing host responses to MARV and Kasokero virus (KASV) using proteomics and viral kinetics, the researchers identified distinct antiviral pathways. Nearly 16% of detected proteins were unique to infected animals, yet canonical inflammatory signatures were absent. MARV induced limited and transient changes, while KASV triggered broader and more sustained responses involving complement, lectin pathways, and hepatometabolic proteins. These findings reveal structured, virus-dependent systemic responses in natural reservoir hosts, offering new insights into viral infection mechanisms. The study's strength lies in its integrative approach, though its focus on captive bats and lack of direct comparisons with other related viruses may limit generalizability.

papers.title_zh: 马尔堡病毒和卡索克罗病毒在自然储存宿主埃及 rousette 蝙蝠中的蛋白质组学比较揭示了不同的通路
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Bats are natural reservoir hosts for numerous zoonotic viruses, yet the molecular mechanisms enabling viral persistence without overt disease remain incompletely understood. The Egyptian rousette bat (Rousettus aegyptiacus, ERB) is the sole known natural reservoir of Marburg virus (MARV) and a key host in the enzootic cycle of the tick-borne Kasokero virus (KASV), providing a unique system to compare host responses to different RNA viruses within the same species. Here, we applied serial cross-sectional serum proteomics integrated with tissue-specific viral kinetics to characterize systemic host responses to experimental MARV and KASV infection in captive-reared bats. Nearly 16 % of detected proteins (67/419) were found exclusively in infected animals, yet canonical acute inflammatory signatures driving pathology in other susceptible hosts were absent (e.g., in humans and non-human primates). Differential abundance and detection analyses identified both shared and virus-dependent responses, with MARV infection eliciting limited and transient perturbations, while KASV induced broader and more sustained engagement of complement, lectin pathway, and hepatometabolic proteins. Network-based analysis uncovered coordinated proteasome modules — including circulating immunoproteasome complexes — consistent with enhanced antigen-processing capacity is a feature of these virus-host dynamics. Together, these findings reveal how ERBs mount structured, virus-dependent systemic responses, offering new insight into mechanisms underlying viral infection in natural reservoir hosts.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 蝙蝠是许多人兽共患病病毒的自然储存宿主,但使病毒能够在不引起明显疾病的情况下持续存在的分子机制仍不完全清楚。埃及 rousette 蝙蝠(Rousettus aegyptiacus,ERB)是马尔堡病毒(MARV)的唯一已知自然储存宿主,也是蜱传播卡索克罗病毒(KASV)在自然循环中的关键宿主,这为在同一物种中比较不同 RNA 病毒的宿主反应提供了独特的系统。在这里,我们应用了连续横断面血清蛋白质组学与组织特异性病毒动力学相结合的方法,以分析实验性 MARV 和 KASV 感染在圈养蝙蝠中的全身宿主反应。检测到的蛋白质中,约有 16 %(67/419)仅在感染动物中发现,但通常与其它易感宿主疾病相关的经典急性炎症标志物却缺失(例如,在人类和非人类灵长类动物中)。差异丰度和检测分析揭示了共同和病毒依赖性的宿主反应,其中 MARV 感染仅引起有限且短暂的扰动,而 KASV 则诱导了更广泛且更持久的补体、凝集素通路以及肝代谢蛋白的参与。基于网络的分析揭示了协调的蛋白酶体模块——包括循环免疫蛋白酶体复合物——这与增强的抗原处理能力是一致的,这可能是这些病毒-宿主动态的一个特征。这些发现表明,埃及 rousette 蝙蝠会针对 MARV 和 KASV 产生结构化的、病毒依赖性的全身反应,为理解自然储存宿主中病毒感染的机制提供了新的见解。

papers.title: EMERGENT AND RE-EMERGENT ZOONOTIC THREATS: CURRENT STATUS, CHALLENGES AND COUNTERACTION STRATEGIES
papers.abstract: The modern world is characterized by the globalization of most processes, accompanied by the speed and scale of change. Over the past 30 years, more than 30 new human pathogens have been identified, 75% of which originated in animals. The emergence of new zoonotic diseases and the resurgence of well-known ones remain a significant challenge for the public health system. The aim of this study is to analyze the current status of emerging and re-emerging zoonotic threats, their epidemic potential, and the necessary countermeasures at the global and national levels. Materials and Methods. An analysis was conducted of official WHO reports (Disease Outbreak News, 2025– July 2026), data from the Global Influenza Surveillance System, and scientific publications in the PubMed and Scopus databases for the period 2016–2026. The bibliosemantic method and descriptive statistics were used. Results and Discussion. Data on current zoonotic infections, including «Disease X» were summarized. The relevance of the issue was demonstrated using the example of outbreaks and epidemics with high mortality rates from 2025 to July 2026. (Marburg disease in Tanzania — 100%, Ebola in the DRC — 70.3%, Nipah disease in Bangladesh — 100%, etc.). The trend in human cases of zoonotic influenza shows an increase in the number of infections with A(H5N1) viruses and the emergence of new viral subtypes (A(H5N5), A(H5N2), A(H9N2)) that are emerging in humans. The need to further implement the «One Health» concept and strengthen national biosafety systems, taking pandemic preparedness into account, has been substantiated. Emerging zoonotic threats remain a priority area for global public health. Effective countermeasures are possible only through strengthened epidemiological surveillance, the development of new diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive measures, the implementation of the «One Health» approach at the national level, and international cooperation, particularly within the framework of the 2025 Pandemic Prevention Agreement. Keywords: emergent infections, re-emergent zoonoses, «Disease X», avian influenza, biosecurity, «One Health», pandemic preparedness.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖描述性统计和文献语义分析,可能无法提供详细的因果见解。然而,证据来源于官方报告和科学文献,支持其结论具有中等置信度。

papers.abstract_zh: 当今世界以大多数过程的全球化为特征,伴随着变化的速度和规模。过去30年中,已识别出超过30种新的人类病原体,其中75%源自动物。新的人兽共患病的出现以及已知疾病的再发仍然是公共卫生体系的重大挑战。本研究旨在分析新兴和再发人兽共患病威胁的现状、其流行潜力以及全球和国家层面所需的应对措施。材料与方法。分析了世界卫生组织(WHO)的官方报告(疾病暴发新闻,2025年7月至2026年7月)、全球流感监测系统数据以及PubMed和Scopus数据库中2016年至2026年的科学文献。采用文献语义分析法和描述性统计方法。结果与讨论。总结了当前人兽共患病感染的数据,包括«疾病X»。通过2025年至2026年7月期间跨物种溢出率高的暴发(如坦桑尼亚的马尔堡病毒病——100%,刚果民主共和国的埃博拉病毒——70.3%,孟加拉国的尼帕病毒病——100%等)来展示该问题的相关性。人兽共患病流感病例的趋势显示,A(H5N1)病毒感染人数增加,同时出现了新的病毒亚型(如A(H5N5)、A(H5N2)、A(H9N2))在人类中出现。进一步实施«一个健康»概念并加强国家生物安全体系,以考虑大流行准备,已被证明是必要的。新兴的人兽共患病威胁仍然是全球公共卫生的优先领域。只有通过加强流行病学监测、开发新的诊断、治疗和预防措施、在国家层面实施«一个健康»方法以及加强国际合作,特别是2025年大流行预防协议框架下的合作,才能实现有效的应对措施。关键词:新兴感染、再发人兽共患病、«疾病X»、禽流感、生物安全、«一个健康»、大流行准备。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究探讨了由新兴和再发人兽共患病带来的挑战,特别是在全球化和越来越多的人类新病原体源自动物的背景下。研究的动机源于对理解并应对这些威胁以保护公共卫生的迫切需求。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了世界卫生组织(WHO)的官方报告、全球流感监测系统数据以及2016年至2026年的科学文献。研究聚焦于当前人兽共患病的现状,包括«疾病X»,并考察了2025年至2026年7月期间跨物种溢出率高的暴发。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用文献语义分析法和描述性统计方法来分析数据,包括对科学文献和官方报告的回顾,以总结人兽共患病的信息及其流行潜力。
analysis_zh.main_results: 本研究指出,过去30年中已识别出超过30种新的病原体,其中75%源自动物。还注意到A(H5N1)病毒在人类中的感染人数增加,同时出现了新的亚型,如A(H5N5)、A(H5N2)和A(H9N2)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者强调,新的人兽共患病的出现以及已知疾病的再发凸显了加强生物安全体系和大流行准备的必要性。本研究有助于理解管理这些威胁的持续挑战。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了加强流行病学监测和实施«一个健康»概念以有效应对人兽共患病威胁的重要性。同时,也强调了为防止大流行而进行国际合作的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究依赖描述性统计和文献语义分析,可能无法提供详细的因果见解。然而,证据来源于官方报告和科学文献,支持其结论具有中等置信度。

systems to improve disease outbreak preparedness and response Ethiopia strengthens laboratory systems to improve disease outbreak preparedness and response 30 September 2026 | Ethiopia Addis Ababa—Humanitarian crises as well as the effects of climate change can increase the risk of infectious disease outbreaks, including diseases that spread from animals to humans, and complicate disease prevention, detection and response efforts. In Ethiopia, where humanitarian crises have left around 22 million people needing urgent assistance, efforts are underway to reinforce the country’s ability to prevent, prepare for, and respond to outbreaks and protect populations. The Ministry of Health, with support from the Pandemic Fund—a financing mechanism to strengthening pandemic prevention, preparedness and response in low- and middle-income countries—and World Health Organization (WHO) is rolling out a national multisectoral project to better integrate human and animal health response systems and enhance key aspects of outbreak preparedness and response, from timely detection to effective implementation. “The Pandemic Fund has three goals. One is to strengthen surveillance. The second is early outbreak investigation and response. The third is capacity building,” says Dr Jarso Debeno, Head of Microbiology at Yabelo Regional Veterinary Laboratory in southern Ethiopia. Strong laboratory systems are essential for timely detection. Between 2024 and 2025, The Pandemic Fund’s support to Ethiopia’s laboratory network improved the detection of priority infectious diseases, including mpox, cholera and Marburg virus disease, and strengthened laboratory quality systems. Laboratory information systems were upgraded, helping to create a more integrated system across human and animal health laboratories. The improved data flow led to a 90% reduction in reporting errors. Molecular testing capacity was also upgraded at eight priority microbiology laboratories. To build the skills of the laboratory workforce, over 1470 laboratory professionals from the human and animal health sectors received training between 2024 and 2026, delivered by project partners Clinton Health Access Initiative and The Animal Health Institute. The training focused on improving diagnostics, genomics, bioinformatics, specimen management, biosafety and quality management systems. Training-of-trainers approaches were used so that learning could duplicated at sub-national levels with a sustainable and long-term approach. “In the past we used to send our samples from Ethiopia to other countries. This is to determine whether there is an outbreak,” says Mebratu Massebo, Chief of Staff at Ethiopia’s Ministry of Health. “But now we have started doing everything ourselves with our own resources.” To support consistent good practices, health authorities developed nine guidelines with standard operating procedures and manuals and these are now in use in sub-national laboratories. More than 40 facilities also received targeted mentorship. Knowledge exchange visits to the United Kingdom, South Africa, Zambia and Kenya also allowed professionals to learn from other countries’ experiences. “There was poor adherence to professional safety when we went into the field in the past,” says Dr Guyo Wenchora, Director of the Yabelo laboratory. “But now, as skills and knowledge have improved, procedures are stronger, work is faster and the quality of work has improved.” The sample output of this laboratory has doubled since 2024. The Ministry of Health has established or upgraded 27 laboratories since 2024. This includes eight new microbiology laboratories for sentinel surveillance, including Yabelo. Sentinel surveillance is a targeted approach to monitoring specific diseases or health events through selected reporting sites, known as sentinel sites. Fifteen public health facilities across 14 regions have been selected as antimicrobial resistance (AMR) sentinel sites, increasing the total number of AMR surveillance laboratories to 41 from 26 in 2023. In addition, four new animal health AMR sites were established and have started testing. “When there is a particular disease outbreak, we go there, we collect samples and we diagnose them immediately, run tests there and provide feedback to the community,” says Dr Guyo. “The contribution of this laboratory to provide rapid response and recommend vaccines and medicines needed to improve animal health is significant.” To ensure these laboratories can function effectively, the project supported a capacity assessment for almost 220 laboratories in 2025. This was conducted alongside the procurement and distribution of essential equipment for more than 430 human health and 20 animal health laboratories. This includes diagnostic equipment, cold-chain systems and transport materials for national and regional laboratories. Around 35 solar-powered refrigerator/freezers have been deployed to veterinary clinics, along with 128 cold boxes distributed to priority districts. The project also continues to support equipment maintenance and covers specimen transportation costs for priority diseases. A total of 267 health facilities in seven regions have procured vans that transport specimens to laboratories for testing, improving timely access to diagnostics and making services more equitable. These sites regularly collect and analyse samples from animals to identify health risks to both animals and humans. In 2025, almost 1000 specimens for priority diseases were transported for testing, including mpox, cholera, and Marburg virus disease. “We have been able to work together to protect the health of people, animals, and the environment,” says Dr Guyo. Aside from co-chairing the Pandemic Fund Steering Committee, WHO plays other key roles in the project. This includes managing the budget and grant for government and delivery partners, leading the UN agencies that are implementing the project, and hosting the project management team at the WHO country office in Addis Ababa. “This project is critical in bringing partners together to advance health emergency preparedness and response in Ethiopia,” says Dr Francis Kasolo, WHO Representative in Ethiopia. “The country is leading with science and WHO is proud to support efforts to ensure that animal, human and environmental health is protected.” Share Related Photo Stories See all → 21 May 2026 Inside WHO Collaborating Centre on HIV Drug Resistance in Botswana 18 September 2025 Kenya strengthens regional disease surveillance through laboratory upgrade 7 June 2024 A Mother’s experience after recovering from Sudan Ebola Virus Disease 1 October 2026 Behind the two drops: The people making every polio vaccination count

news.content_zh: 埃塞俄比亚一直在加强其实验室系统,以提高疾病 暴发 的应对和响应能力,特别是针对优先传染病如 马尔堡病毒病。这一倡议由大流行基金和世界卫生组织(WHO)支持,包括自2024年以来建立和升级了27个实验室,其中8个新的微生物学实验室用于哨点 监测。该项目提高了分子检测能力,将报告错误率降低了90%,并培训了超过1470名专业人员在诊断、生物信息学和生物安全领域。此外,七个地区内的267个卫生设施已采购运输车以改善样本运输和检测。卫生部已制定标准操作程序和指南,超过40个设施已获得针对性指导。该倡议还包括采购关键设备,如诊断工具和冷链系统,并在兽医诊所部署太阳能冷藏箱。这些努力旨在建立更整合的人类和动物健康响应系统,从而实现更快、更准确的 暴发 检测,并改善公共卫生成果。

Limited (ASX:ILA) Starts GMP Galidesivir Manufacturing for Ebola and Marburg Programs Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) Starts GMP Galidesivir Manufacturing for Ebola and Marburg Programs Sonal Highlights Island Pharmaceuticals has commenced GMP manufacture of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient, with production beginning on 1 October 2026. The first 5kg GMP batch is targeted for completion by the end of October and is intended for an approved emergency-use program in Uganda. A second 5kg batch is scheduled for completion by late November to support broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The Manufacturing program also includes analytical validation, reference-standard preparation and stability studies. Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) is an Australian antiviral Drug Development and biodefence company focused on therapies addressing viral diseases, public-health needs and biosecurity threats. Its development portfolio includes ISLA-101 and Galidesivir, a clinical-stage broad-spectrum antiviral with activity across more than 20 RNA viruses. The company has now moved Galidesivir into GMP manufacturing, establishing drug Supply for planned Ebola and Marburg development programs. First Galidesivir GMP Batch Enters Production Island reported that GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient began on 1 October at PI Health Sciences. The manufacturing campaign marks the transition of its expanded Galidesivir program into physical production. The first batch is expected to produce 5kg of GMP-grade API by the end of October 2026. Island has earmarked this material for its approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. After API production is completed, additional finishing, vialing and packaging work will be required before the product can be shipped for investigational therapeutic use. The proposed deployment will operate under the World Health Organization's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions framework. Emergency Program Could Generate Human Clinical Data The emergency-use program is intended to involve prospective collection of clinical, safety and virological data from patients treated with Galidesivir. This represents a different evidence stream from the company's existing preclinical work. Island stated that Galidesivir already has human clinical experience as well as historical efficacy data from non-human primate models of Ebola and Marburg virus disease. The company is seeking to build on that development history through two parallel pathways: prospective human data collection in Ebola under the MEURI framework and controlled non-human primate studies in Marburg under the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Animal Rule pathway. The announcement does not provide efficacy outcomes from the current emergency-use program because treatment and data collection have not yet been completed. Second 5kg Batch Supports Marburg Development Island is targeting completion of a second 5kg GMP API batch by the end of November 2026. This material is intended to support the company's broader Ebola development strategy as well as its planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The Marburg program is being developed under the FDA Animal Rule, which provides a regulatory pathway for certain products where human efficacy studies are not ethical or feasible. Together, the two planned campaigns represent 10kg of targeted GMP API production. The first allocation is aimed at near-term emergency-use requirements, while the second is directed toward additional development activity. Manufacturing Program Extends Beyond API Production The broader manufacturing program includes analytical method validation, preparation of reference standards and stability studies. These activities are intended to establish the manufacturing and quality framework required for continued Galidesivir development. Island also stated that the program is designed to support potential outbreak deployment, future regulatory activity and possible government procurement. These remain prospective objectives rather than completed commercial agreements. Galidesivir has previously benefited from more than US$70 million of U.S. Government investment, according to the company. Island is now using the current manufacturing campaign to create GMP-grade supply that can be used across its planned clinical and regulatory programs. Ebola Outbreak Provides Immediate Development Context The company cited World Health Organization data showing that, as of 27 September 2026, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak had resulted in 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths. This equates to a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48%. Island noted that there is no approved specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, forming the public-health context for the planned investigational deployment of Galidesivir. Key Takeaway Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) has moved Galidesivir into GMP production, with two 5kg batches planned across October and November 2026. The first batch is intended for an Ebola emergency-use program in Uganda, while the second is earmarked for broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The next major milestones are completion of manufacturing, shipment preparation and subsequent generation of clinical and preclinical data. FAQs Q: What has Island Pharmaceuticals started manufacturing? A: Island has commenced GMP manufacture of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient. Q: How much Galidesivir is being produced? A: Two 5kg GMP API batches are planned, giving a targeted total of 10kg. Q: What will the first batch be used for? A: The first batch is earmarked for Island's approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. Q: What is the purpose of the second batch? A: It is intended to support broader Ebola development and a planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. Q: When are the batches expected to be completed? A: The first batch is targeted for completion by the end of October 2026 and the second by the end of November 2026. Limited (ASX:ILA) Starts GMP Galidesivir Manufacturing for Ebola and Marburg Programs Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) Starts GMP Galidesivir Manufacturing for Ebola and Marburg Programs Sonal Highlights Island Pharmaceuticals has commenced GMP manufacture of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient, with production beginning on 1 October 2026. The first 5kg GMP batch is targeted for completion by the end of October and is intended for an approved emergency-use program in Uganda. A second 5kg batch is scheduled for completion by late November to support broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The Manufacturing program also includes analytical validation, reference-standard preparation and stability studies. Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) is an Australian antiviral Drug Development and biodefence company focused on therapies addressing viral diseases, public-health needs and biosecurity threats. Its development portfolio includes ISLA-101 and Galidesivir, a clinical-stage broad-spectrum antiviral with activity across more than 20 RNA viruses. The company has now moved Galidesivir into GMP manufacturing, establishing drug Supply for planned Ebola and Marburg development programs. First Galidesivir GMP Batch Enters Production Island reported that GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient began on 1 October at PI Health Sciences. The manufacturing campaign marks the transition of its expanded Galidesivir program into physical production. The first batch is expected to produce 5kg of GMP-grade API by the end of October 2026. Island has earmarked this material for its approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. After API production is completed, additional finishing, vialing and packaging work will be required before the product can be shipped for investigational therapeutic use. The proposed deployment will operate under the World Health Organization's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions framework. Emergency Program Could Generate Human Clinical Data The emergency-use program is intended to involve prospective collection of clinical, safety and virological data from patients treated with Galidesivir. This represents a different evidence stream from the company's existing preclinical work. Island stated that Galidesivir already has human clinical experience as well as historical efficacy data from non-human primate models of Ebola and Marburg virus disease. The company is seeking to build on that development history through two parallel pathways: prospective human data collection in Ebola under the MEURI framework and controlled non-human primate studies in Marburg under the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Animal Rule pathway. The announcement does not provide efficacy outcomes from the current emergency-use program because treatment and data collection have not yet been completed. Second 5kg Batch Supports Marburg Development Island is targeting completion of a second 5kg GMP API batch by the end of November 2026. This material is intended to support the company's broader Ebola development strategy as well as its planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The Marburg program is being developed under the FDA Animal Rule, which provides a regulatory pathway for certain products where human efficacy studies are not ethical or feasible. Together, the two planned campaigns represent 10kg of targeted GMP API production. The first allocation is aimed at near-term emergency-use requirements, while the second is directed toward additional development activity. Manufacturing Program Extends Beyond API Production The broader manufacturing program includes analytical method validation, preparation of reference standards and stability studies. These activities are intended to establish the manufacturing and quality framework required for continued Galidesivir development. Island also stated that the program is designed to support potential outbreak deployment, future regulatory activity and possible government procurement. These remain prospective objectives rather than completed commercial agreements. Galidesivir has previously benefited from more than US$70 million of U.S. Government investment, according to the company. Island is now using the current manufacturing campaign to create GMP-grade supply that can be used across its planned clinical and regulatory programs. Ebola Outbreak Provides Immediate Development Context The company cited World Health Organization data showing that, as of 27 September 2026, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak had resulted in 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths. This equates to a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48%. Island noted that there is no approved specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, forming the public-health context for the planned investigational deployment of Galidesivir. Key Takeaway Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) has moved Galidesivir into GMP production, with two 5kg batches planned across October and November 2026. The first batch is intended for an Ebola emergency-use program in Uganda, while the second is earmarked for broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The next major milestones are completion of manufacturing, shipment preparation and subsequent generation of clinical and preclinical data. FAQs Q: What has Island Pharmaceuticals started manufacturing? A: Island has commenced GMP manufacture of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient. Q: How much Galidesivir is being produced? A: Two 5kg GMP API batches are planned, giving a targeted total of 10kg. Q: What will the first batch be used for? A: The first batch is earmarked for Island's approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. Q: What is the purpose of the second batch? A: It is intended to support broader Ebola development and a planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. Q: When are the batches expected to be completed? A: The first batch is targeted for completion by the end of October 2026 and the second by the end of November 2026. news.content_zh: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) 已启动其埃博拉和马尔堡开发项目的GMP加德西维瑞制造。预计第一批次5公斤将在2026年10月底完成,用于乌干达正在进行的邦迪布古埃博拉暴发的紧急使用计划。第二批次5公斤预计于2026年11月下旬完成,以支持更广泛的埃博拉开发和一项关键的马尔堡非人灵长类动物研究。该制造计划包括分析验证、参考标准制备和稳定性研究,以建立持续开发的质量框架。紧急使用计划将在世界卫生组织的《未注册和研究性干预措施的监测紧急使用》框架下进行,而马尔堡项目则在FDA动物规则下开发。公司尚未提供当前紧急使用计划的疗效结果,因为治疗和数据收集尚未完成。这标志着从临床前研究向实际生产过渡,旨在为临床和监管项目创建GMP级供应。

Island Pharmaceuticals (ASX:ILA) disclosed that good manufacturing practice (GMP) manufacture of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) commenced on 1 October 2026 at PI Health Sciences (PIHS), marking the start of physical production under the company's expanded manufacturing program. Key Points GMP manufacture of Galidesivir API commenced on 1 October 2026 at PI Health Sciences First 5kg GMP API batch targeted for completion by the end of October 2026, earmarked for Island's approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the current Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak Second 5kg GMP API batch targeted for completion by late November 2026, intended to support Island's broader Ebola strategy and planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study under the FDA Animal Rule The ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak had resulted in 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths as at 27 September 2026, representing a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48% Galidesivir has been authorised for investigational therapeutic use under the WHO MEURI framework, with prospective clinical, safety and virological data to be collected from treated patients First GMP Batch and Emergency-Use Program in Uganda The multi-step manufacturing process is now underway, with the first 5kg batch of GMP-grade Galidesivir API targeted for completion by the end of October 2026. This batch has been earmarked to support Island's approved emergency-use program during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. Following completion of API manufacture, Island disclosed it will undertake the required finishing, vialing and packaging activities ahead of planned shipment to Uganda for investigational therapeutic use under the World Health Organization's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions (MEURI) framework. Treatment under MEURI will occur under a prospective protocol, enabling collection of clinical, safety and virological data from patients treated with Galidesivir. Second Batch to Support Ebola Strategy and Marburg NHP Study A second 5kg GMP API batch is targeted for completion by the end of November 2026. According to the filing, this additional supply is intended to support Island's broader Ebola strategy and to provide material for the company's planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study under the US Food and Drug Administration's Animal Rule pathway. Manufacturing is being undertaken at PIHS under the company's existing agreement. The broader program also encompasses analytical method validation, reference standard preparation and stability studies, establishing the manufacturing and quality framework required to support Galidesivir's continued development, potential outbreak deployment and future regulatory and government procurement activities. Galidesivir Development Background and Bundibugyo Outbreak Data The filing states that Galidesivir has benefited from more than US$70 million of prior US Government investment and has existing human clinical experience together with historical efficacy data in non-human primate models of Ebola and Marburg virus disease. The ongoing Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus had resulted in 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths as at 27 September 2026, representing a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48%, according to the latest available WHO data cited in the filing. The filing notes the absence of an approved specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease. Pharmaceuticals Commences GMP Manufacturing of Galidesivir to Support Ebola and Marburg Programs Island Pharmaceuticals Commences GMP Manufacturing of Galidesivir to Support Ebola and Marburg Programs Island Pharmaceuticals (ASX:ILA) disclosed that good manufacturing practice (GMP) manufacture of Galidesivir active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) commenced on 1 October 2026 at PI Health Sciences (PIHS), marking the start of physical production under the company's expanded manufacturing program. Key Points GMP manufacture of Galidesivir API commenced on 1 October 2026 at PI Health Sciences First 5kg GMP API batch targeted for completion by the end of October 2026, earmarked for Island's approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the current Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak Second 5kg GMP API batch targeted for completion by late November 2026, intended to support Island's broader Ebola strategy and planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study under the FDA Animal Rule The ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak had resulted in 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths as at 27 September 2026, representing a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48% Galidesivir has been authorised for investigational therapeutic use under the WHO MEURI framework, with prospective clinical, safety and virological data to be collected from treated patients First GMP Batch and Emergency-Use Program in Uganda The multi-step manufacturing process is now underway, with the first 5kg batch of GMP-grade Galidesivir API targeted for completion by the end of October 2026. This batch has been earmarked to support Island's approved emergency-use program during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. Following completion of API manufacture, Island disclosed it will undertake the required finishing, vialing and packaging activities ahead of planned shipment to Uganda for investigational therapeutic use under the World Health Organization's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions (MEURI) framework. Treatment under MEURI will occur under a prospective protocol, enabling collection of clinical, safety and virological data from patients treated with Galidesivir. Second Batch to Support Ebola Strategy and Marburg NHP Study A second 5kg GMP API batch is targeted for completion by the end of November 2026. According to the filing, this additional supply is intended to support Island's broader Ebola strategy and to provide material for the company's planned pivotal Marburg non-human primate study under the US Food and Drug Administration's Animal Rule pathway. Manufacturing is being undertaken at PIHS under the company's existing agreement. The broader program also encompasses analytical method validation, reference standard preparation and stability studies, establishing the manufacturing and quality framework required to support Galidesivir's continued development, potential outbreak deployment and future regulatory and government procurement activities. Galidesivir Development Background and Bundibugyo Outbreak Data The filing states that Galidesivir has benefited from more than US$70 million of prior US Government investment and has existing human clinical experience together with historical efficacy data in non-human primate models of Ebola and Marburg virus disease. The ongoing Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus had resulted in 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths as at 27 September 2026, representing a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48%, according to the latest available WHO data cited in the filing. The filing notes the absence of an approved specific treatment for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease. news.content_zh: Island Pharmaceuticals 于 2026 年 10 月 1 日在 PI Health Sciences 开始 Galidesivir API 的 GMP 生产,以支持其在乌干达应对持续的 Bundibugyo 埃博拉 暴发 的紧急使用计划。预计第一批次 5kg 将于 2026 年 10 月底完成,第二批次 5kg 将于 2026 年 11 月下旬完成,以协助更广泛的埃博拉战略和 FDA 动物规则下的计划马尔堡非人灵长类动物研究。截至 2026 年 9 月 27 日,Bundibugyo 暴发 已报告 8,137 例确诊病例和 3,926 例确认死亡病例,病死率约为 48%。Galidesivir 在 WHO MEURI 框架下被授权用于研究性使用,允许收集临床、安全性和病毒学结果的数据。目前尚无针对 Bundibugyo 埃博拉病毒病的获批特定 治疗,突显了这一进展的重要性。公司将在发货前完成成品、装瓶和包装工作。这一行动是更大计划的一部分,包括分析方法验证、参考标准制备和稳定性研究,以支持 Galidesivir 的开发和潜在监管采购。
